plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Before a single leaf unfurls, the bare branches of the Yoshino cherry fill with clouds of blush-white, softly fragrant blossoms. Along riverbanks and city avenues, the petals drift down like pink snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April, with peak bloom usually from late March to early April and often lingering into the first part of April
plants.location: Washington, D.C., USA, and other temperate parts of the Northern Hemisphere (native to Japan)
plants.funFact: The Yoshino cherry is a hybrid, so its seeds don't reliably grow true to type. Cherry trees are propagated by grafting, which means many trees lining a street are genetic clones of one another and tend to bloom in near-perfect unison.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Row upon row of cup-shaped blooms turn the Dutch countryside into a patchwork of crimson, gold, magenta and white stripes. Their glossy petals open wide in the afternoon sun and close up again as the evening cools.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-May, usually at its best in mid-April
plants.location: The Netherlands, including the bulb fields and gardens around Keukenhof
plants.funFact: Tulips are native to the mountains of Central Asia, not Holland. In the 17th century they sparked 'tulip mania', when single bulbs sold for more than the price of a house.

plants.name: Lupinus texensis
plants.description: Each spring, Texas roadsides and meadows flood with waves of deep blue-violet lupine spikes. The tips of the flower stalks are dabbed with white, like a paintbrush dipped in snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March through April, with peak bloom in late March and early April
plants.funFact: Texas has five official state flowers, all of them bluebonnet species. The white tip on each bloom turns magenta-red as the flower is pollinated, a signal to bees that it has already been visited.
